top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a bounded, identifiable invention: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice, which cancels the clock-transition light shift while many atoms are interrogated in Lamb-Dicke confinement, and Ye's group taking strontium lattice clocks to the 10^-18 regime. It is reproduced and surpassed by independent laboratories and already used for redshift tests and bounds on varying constants and dark matter. The two-name credit divides cleanly and a narrow citation keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is mature science but its three-name credit omits the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal and the 3D work, so it ranks second; no award is last because a mature, defensible prize is available.
recusal_note: No direct connection to the P001 or P002 laureates apparent from profile; Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize and I work in superconducting circuits, but neither bears on these proposals.
